lessons.title: Introduction to Python

lessons.title: Numbers and Numeric Operations
lessons.overview: Python provides int, float and complex numeric types. Arithmetic operators include +, -, *, /, //, %, and **; true division returns a float. Operator precedence matters, and floating-point arithmetic can involve representation error.
lessons.code:
marks = [72, 84, 91]
average = sum(marks) / len(marks)
print(round(average, 2))
print(17 // 5, 17 % 5, 2 ** 5)
lessons.application: Compute aggregate marks and basic statistical summaries.
lessons.tip: Never compare floating-point results for exact equality when tolerance is needed.

scores.sort(reverse=True)

lessons.tip: Beware of aliasing: a = b does not copy a list.

lessons.title: Namespaces and Scope
lessons.overview: Python resolves variable names using local, enclosing, global and built-in scopes (LEGB). global and nonlocal alter assignments across scope boundaries; avoid hidden dependencies when possible.
lessons.code:

    count = 0
    def increment():
        nonlocal count
        count += 1
        return count
    return increment
next_count = outer()
print(next_count(), next_count())
lessons.application: Encapsulate counters and state in closures.
lessons.tip: An assignment inside a function normally creates a local name.
